title: A Bid From a Dublin Bar and Digicel's First 100 Days in Jamaica
conflicts: Early subscribers: the Jamaica Observer (2010) says the founders' model put the market's outer limit at 100,000 handsets for the first full year, and quotes O'Brien that 300,000 'would be wonderful' and that the first year's target was passed within months; in USA Today (2006) O'Brien claims 100,000 subscribers within 100 days. No operator or regulator figure found; the story gives the model and the 100-day figure as O'Brien's claim. Overtaking Cable & Wireless: 'eleven months later' (O'Brien, USA Today, ambiguous), so the story says 'not long afterwards, he said'. Licence: April 2000 auction (Irish Times 2005) vs won in June 2000 (RTE 2001); $47.5m (RTE, Irish Times) vs US$47m (Observer); story says 2000 and about $47.5m. Investment: US$100m budgeted (O'Brien), $180m (RTE at launch), over US$177m (RCR 2001), $150m initial (Irish Times 2005); story uses only the budgeted figure, attributed. Pre-launch mobile penetration 4% (USA Today), 7% (RTE), about 10% (Irish Times); not used.
notes: Moriarty Tribunal not mentioned; the story keeps to the 2000-01 bid and launch. Launch date 19 April 2001 rests on RTE's same-day report and Jean Lowrie-Chin's first-hand recollection (a blog excerpt of her Jamaica Observer column). The USA Today article is cited at its usatoday30 archive address because the www address now 404s.
